The Preserve is the clearest local expression of Peril to Profit: danger is real, but so are the people and creatures living around it; the corporations mostly learned how to meter, brand, and bill the crossing. Hundred-foot trunks, sunken roads, dense canopy-dark, blue river-glow, warning placards, mosslit root doors, and cheerful liability language weathering on old wood. Player Display Caption: A vast ancient forest with trees wider than a carriage, older than any company sign.
Manufactured Threat: Hazard sightings and protection pricing have risen together year over year. The forest is framed as danger while its own old magic still keeps people alive.

An ancient forest logistics preserve where colossal trees, hybrid fauna, underroot communities, route tolls, and corporate liability language all compete to define what safety means. Sablewood is an ancient forest forced to wear a logistics badge: colossal trunks, liability signs, toll language, and living routes that do not care about forms. Sablewood is a national-forest-scale wilderness wearing a branded vest it did not ask for. The trees are huge enough to drive wagons through hollow roots; the road is an agreement, not a conquest. The place breaks into usable table spaces: Managed carriage road: A wet road threads between trunks the size of small houses. Root underpasses: Hollow roots create side tunnels, animal shade, and places a cart cannot follow. Waymarker clearings: Cheerful route markers and supply posts look tiny...
